concerns: LEGION-76 (cross-issue new-session lane) edits the same has-session/new-session step inside openWindow; keep ensureSession one function so its lane can wrap it, and expect a textual conflict in openWindow's body for whichever pull request lands second.

retireAndRespawnStuckController returns without spawning when the controller is found already dead at the deadline (controllerAlive() clears the locator; `if (!stillAlive) return`), and nothing periodic calls ensureController — a dead-before-registering controller stays absent until an Envoy no-holder exception or a restart. Outside this issue; worth its own LEGION issue.

The workspace's working copy holds an untracked-by-intent `.omp/config.yml` written by provisioning; commit only your own paths with `jj split <paths>` and set the bookmark on the described commit, never the bare working copy.
A rig started from a worker pane inherits that pane's LEGION_* identity (LEGION-88) and its controller never registers; the rig recipe scrubs those variables before up.sh.

The rig's 15 s registration deadline retires every controller that has not registered within 15 s, so the retire/respawn cycle repeats until one registers first; each rig start yields at least the boot controller's cycle — restart the rig for more.
summary: When a stuck controller whose window is the private tmux session's only window is retired, tmux tears down the session and server; the respawn's has-session can still answer present and its new-window then fails on a dead server, leaving no controller. Fix in openWindow (tmux.ts): on a new-window failure after has-session said present, run the session-ensuring step again — if it had to create the session, retry new-window once and report the recovery for the runtime to log; if the session is still there, or this call created it, fail as today. Every tmux.ts failure message ends with tmux's stderr or `tmux printed nothing on stderr`.
verifiedFacts: At incident head 9a6708fe openWindow printed stdout (empty on failure); LEGION-74 (2553ca37) already switched every tmux.ts message to stderr via failure(). The incident's tmux stderr is therefore unknown; the fix decides by re-asking tmux, not by wording.
stderr reaches failure(): state/fetch.ts defaultRunner pipes stderr and returns it; environment.ts createDaemonRunner passes the result through; index.ts hands that runner to TmuxRuntime as tmux.run.

Race window: TmuxRuntime.stop confirms a graceful stop when the shim socket closes; worker-shim stops its listener the instant OMP exits, before Bun exits, before the pane's shell exits, before tmux reaps pane -> window -> session -> server (exit-empty). kill-pane is synchronous: on tmux 3.7c has-session right after kill-pane of the last pane answers `no server running on <socket>`.

tmux 3.7c stderr shapes (measured): server gone `no server running on /tmp/tmux-1000/<socket>`; socket never created `error connecting to … (No such file or directory)`; server alive/session gone: new-window says `can't find window: <s>`, has-session says `can't find session: <s>`; second new-session `duplicate session: <s>`; new-session on a stale socket starts a fresh server (exit 0).
Baseline green: bun test tmux.test.ts runtime.contract.test.ts -> 93 pass after `bun install` in the workspace.

design.tmux.ts: Split openWindow into ensureSession(server, session, owner): Promise<boolean> (has-session; else the existing single-invocation new-session + set-option update-environment '' and the session owner marker; returns whether this call created it) and newWindowAttempt(server, session, name, environmentAndCommand, created) (new-window -P -F; when created, kill the bootstrap window afterwards whatever the outcome). openWindow: ensure -> attempt; on non-zero exit: if created, throw the first error as today; else created = await ensureSession(...) again — if it returns false (session still there) throw the first error as today; else attempt once more — on success return { windowId, paneId, pid, recovered: <first error text> }, on failure throw `tmux new-window failed (exit N)<stderr> on the second attempt, after has-session reported <session> present and then gone (first attempt: <first error>)`. failure() returns `: <stderr>` or `: tmux printed nothing on stderr`. Export interface OpenedWindow { windowId; paneId; pid; recovered?: string }.
design.runtime-tmux.ts: Private openWindow(name, paneArgv) helper used by spawnIssueProcess and spawnController: calls tmux.openWindow(this.deps.tmux, session, name, paneArgv, session) and, when recovered is set, console.error(`[legion] tmux new-window for ${name} failed after has-session reported ${session} present, and the session was gone by the time the window opened (${recovered}); recreated it and opened the window on a second attempt`).
design.processes.ts: No product change: the `[legion] failed to retire and respawn a stuck controller:` line prints the thrown Error, whose message now always ends with stderr or the explicit empty-stderr note. Tests only.
rejected: Blind retry on any new-window failure (doubles attempt counts existing processes tests pin; re-runs unrelated failures).
Waiting in stop() for the pane to vanish (spec asks for the fall-back; a poll on every stop; misses a server that died for another reason).
Classifying by stderr wording (differs by case/version; asking tmux again is the direct test).
Logging from tmux.ts (module returns details, runtime logs — lookupPane precedent).
Re-arming a timer in retireAndRespawnStuckController on a failed respawn (new state; spec rules it out; second failure is an error by the spec's table).
